Ggz_gd--UO0.summary: Justice Antonin Scalia's opening statement at a 2011 Senate Judiciary hearing on the role of judges. He argues that the Constitution's separation of powers is what protects liberty, and that gridlock is by design.
Ggz_gd--UO0.why: Recommended often as a clear explanation of why the US system is built to be slow and why gridlock protects minorities.

GJCF-Ufapu8.summary: A compilation of the 1977 BBC series The Secret War, a documentary on British scientific and technical efforts in WWII, including radar, German navigation beams and V-weapons. It features interviews with people who were there, including Albert Speer.
GJCF-Ufapu8.why: HN readers recommend it as a detailed, intelligent documentary about wartime technology that assumes viewers aren't stupid.

GvtNyOzGogc.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on Sinclair Broadcast Group, the largest owner of US local TV stations, and how it injects political content and scripted must-run segments into local news.
GvtNyOzGogc.why: HN repeatedly points to it as the eye-opening explanation of media consolidation and scripted local news.

Ge3aKEmZcqY.summary: Casey Muratori's University of Twente guest lecture is a case study in how straightforward code can cut thousands of lines and tens of seconds of runtime down to a few dozen lines running in under a second. It uses concrete examples to show why software is often an order of magnitude slower than it should be.
Ge3aKEmZcqY.why: HN people recommend it to anyone wanting a practical sense of what CPUs can really do and why abstraction layers cost so much performance.

GiYO1TObNz8.summary: Technology Connections explains how LED traffic lights, which do not melt snow, drew complaints and were blamed for accidents. He uses it to illustrate the 'but sometimes' fallacy against new technology.
GiYO1TObNz8.why: Cited constantly as the name and example of the 'but sometimes' argument, where edge cases are used to resist better technology such as EVs and solar.

Gv2I7qTux7g.summary: Zig creator Andrew Kelley justifies why Zig exists and tours its distinctive features, including C interoperability and comptime, along with what people had built and what 1.0 would bring. It was given at Philly ETE 2019.
Gv2I7qTux7g.why: HN treats it as the standard introduction to Zig by its creator, with some calling it among the best talks they have seen.

G1r55efei5c.summary: A short !!Con 2016 talk by blind developer Sina Bahram on how he uses a computer and writes code with a screen reader at about 1,000 words per minute. He plays how common interfaces sound and challenges the audience to go a day using only the keyboard.
G1r55efei5c.why: HN commenters repeatedly share it because it is an eye-opening look at screen-reader use, and because at about 6:30 it addresses how inaccessible Hacker News itself is.

GOGru_4z1Vc.summary: Kurt Vonnegut's 2004 Case College lecture, with Spanish subtitles, in which he sketches the shapes of stories on a blackboard. He plots story arcs as good and bad fortune against time.
GOGru_4z1Vc.why: Frequently recommended as a delightful, influential way to think about story structure.

G_eYTctGZw8.summary: Michael Hendricks of PriceCharting shares tricks and pain points from running Prolog in production for 18 months at Strange Loop. It argues Prolog is a productive modern language beyond logic puzzles, and includes a demo of changing code mid-execution.
G_eYTctGZw8.why: It is the go-to answer to whether Prolog is used for real-world work, praised as a survey of its uses, advantages and drawbacks.

GuigptwlVHo.summary: Numberphile talks with mathematician Ron Graham about the magnitude of Graham's number, building up from arrow notation to show how impossibly large it is. It is part of a series of videos on this number.
GuigptwlVHo.why: HN commenters recommend it for hearing Graham himself and for its clear introduction to up-arrow notation and enormous numbers.

Gatn5ameRr8.summary: Jonathan Haidt's Hayek Lecture at Duke argues American universities pursue two potentially incompatible sacred values, truth and social justice. He discusses campus conflict, honor, dignity and victimhood cultures, and viewpoint diversity.
Gatn5ameRr8.why: HN cites it heavily in diversity and academia debates as an intellectual analysis of the truth versus social justice conflict.

G0R09YzyuCI.summary: Joseph Tainter lectures at a 2010 sustainability conference on why complex societies such as Rome collapse. His thesis is that rising complexity brings diminishing returns until societies cannot afford to maintain it.
G0R09YzyuCI.why: Recommended as the best exposition of Tainter's theory, and used to explain slowing innovation, centralization and collapse risk.

GNO_CYUjMK8.summary: Steven Wittens' JSConf US 2013 talk on drawing with WebGL, using animated visuals to walk through vectors, matrices and the rendering pipeline. Despite the title, it works as a visual primer on the linear algebra behind 3D graphics.
GNO_CYUjMK8.why: HN treats it as one of the best intros to the math of 3D graphics and a staple answer to how to learn graphics programming.

GVsUOuSjvcg.summary: Veritasium explains why analog computing may suit AI workloads, covering old analog computers, The Analog Thing and Mythic's analog chips that use flash memory for neural network inference. It argues digital hardware is hitting limits.
GVsUOuSjvcg.why: Treated as the accessible reference on analog computing for neural nets, especially the Mythic AI segment.

GnBbhXBDmwU.summary: Bob Beck of OpenBSD describes the first month of LibreSSL, the fork aimed at cleaning up OpenSSL, including oddities found in the code base and why it was cleaned rather than audited cryptographically.
GnBbhXBDmwU.why: Frequently linked as an entertaining and alarming account of OpenSSL code quality and why the fork happened.

GoW8Tf7hTGA.summary: A visual scale comparison of stars and cosmic objects, from planets up to some of the largest known stars, set to music. It is meant to convey the vastness of the universe.
GoW8Tf7hTGA.why: Shared as a go-to humbling look at cosmic scale, noted for its chilling audio and visuals pairing.

GqmsQeSzMdw.summary: Runar Bjarnason's Scala World talk argues that restraint and precision in components beat power and flexibility. Constraints on parts make them easier to compose into systems.
GqmsQeSzMdw.why: HN recommends it as a talk that changes how you think about system design, and links it whenever constraints, abstraction or least power come up.

G0Cp7DrvNLQ.summary: A three-hour Joe Rogan podcast with Randall Carlson, builder and geomythologist, on catastrophic geological events, cosmic impacts and climate at the end of the last glacial period.
G0Cp7DrvNLQ.why: Commenters in climate and impact-event threads send people to Carlson's Rogan appearances for his account of ancient cataclysms.

GTQnarzmTOc.summary: A hip-hop music video from EconStories in which Keynes and Hayek rap-battle over how to handle recessions and government spending. It is the second round after the first rap battle.
GTQnarzmTOc.why: Offered as a quick, entertaining primer on Keynesian versus Austrian economics, especially for newcomers to Hayek.

GWQh_DmDLKQ.summary: X.Org developer Daniel Stone explains the history and technical limits of the X Window System and why Wayland was created, debunking myths from forum comments. He covers topics such as network transparency and blocking calls.
GWQh_DmDLKQ.why: HN uses it as the go-to answer to claims that Wayland is unnecessary, from a developer who knew X's codebase well.

G8cbIWMv0rI.summary: A short clip from Carl Sagan's Cosmos in which he explains how Eratosthenes measured the circumference of the Earth using shadows in two Egyptian cities. It is a clear, visual account of an ancient scientific feat.
G8cbIWMv0rI.why: HN commenters link it whenever the question of how the Earth's size was first measured comes up, calling it a wonderful explanation.

GcJxRqTs5nk.summary: Frans de Waal's TED talk shows videos of behavioral experiments on primates and other mammals that reveal empathy, cooperation, fairness and reciprocity. He argues these moral traits are not uniquely human.
GcJxRqTs5nk.why: Commenters call it a must-watch, funny and entertaining demonstration that morality has natural roots in animals.

GhsZUZmJvaM.summary: Veritasium's Derek Muller visits NASA JPL to see the Mars helicopter Ingenuity before it was mounted on the rover. He explains how it can fly in Mars's thin atmosphere with large, fast-spinning contra-rotating rotors and low mass, and covers power and cold.
GhsZUZmJvaM.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as an excellent explanation of why flying on Mars is hard and how the helicopter was built.

GoJsr4IwCm4.summary: Kurzgesagt's short animated video asks whether humanity should try to end aging, and argues the case for curing age-related disease. It is part one of a pair, with a second part by CGP Grey.
GoJsr4IwCm4.why: HN commenters recommend it as a compelling, concise argument for longevity research and a rebuttal to common objections to ending aging.

G-WO-z-QuWI.summary: Kurzgesagt lays out a speculative plan to terraform Venus, covering its hostile atmosphere and how it might be made Earth-like, with a sources page linked.
G-WO-z-QuWI.why: Offered as a readable explainer whenever Venus terraforming or alternatives to Mars colonization come up.

G0ZZJXw4MTA.summary: A clip from Yes Prime Minister in which Sir Humphrey shows how leading questions can make a survey support or oppose national service. It is a short satirical scene.
G0ZZJXw4MTA.why: HN commenters bring it up whenever a poll or survey result looks suspect, as the classic illustration of biased question framing.

GtQdIYUtAHg.summary: Viznut demonstrates bytebeat, experimental music generated by extremely short C programs. It is the first of a series of videos on the technique.
GtQdIYUtAHg.why: HN calls it the video that started the one-line-code music trend and recommends exploring the demoscene author's channel.

G0Q4UAiKacw.summary: A PBS Space Time episode on how the Higgs mechanism gives particles mass, prompted by Fermilab's heavier-than-expected W boson measurement. It goes beyond the usual pop-science treatment without heavy math.
G0Q4UAiKacw.why: HN recommends it as the best non-mathematical explanation of the Higgs field, deep but accessible to lay viewers.

GFosQtEqzSE.summary: David MacKay, scientific advisor to the UK energy department, gives a Harvard talk on sustainable energy at macro and micro scale, drawn from his book Sustainable Energy Without the Hot Air. It stresses the land area renewables require.
GFosQtEqzSE.why: HN recommends it as an approachable, numbers-driven overview of what renewable energy would take.

GLG9g7BcjKs.summary: Jonathan Pie delivers a satirical rant just after the 2016 US election, blaming the political and media establishment for the rise of Trump. It is a short, profane monologue in character as a frustrated reporter.
GLG9g7BcjKs.why: Shared after the 2016 election and later as a pithy account of why Trump won and why political division needs to be moved past.

GNKFSpJIBO0.summary: Mathematician Colin Wright demonstrates juggling and explains the mathematics of juggling patterns, including notation that led to new throwing patterns. It is a public presentation at the Museum of Mathematics aimed at a general audience.
GNKFSpJIBO0.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining way to learn math through juggling.

GRYcSuyLiJk.summary: A 73-minute Stanford talk by Robert Sapolsky drawn from his book Behave. It surveys the biological factors behind human behavior at its best and worst.
GRYcSuyLiJk.why: HN recommends Sapolsky as an exceptional storyteller and points to this lecture on the biology of human behavior and violence.

GVT3WUa-48Y.summary: Corridor Digital makes a roughly seven-minute anime short using Stable Diffusion and related AI tools, based on a technique they teach in a longer tutorial. It was an early showcase of AI-assisted animation.
GVT3WUa-48Y.why: HN commenters point to it as an impressive example of what AI animation could do and of VFX artists adopting AI in their workflows.

G1m0aX9Lpts.summary: Sam Aaron live codes an ambient electronic set using Sonic Pi, the music programming environment he created. The performance shows code driving music in real time.
G1m0aX9Lpts.why: Offered as an example of live-coded music and a fun entry point to Sonic Pi.

G4hL5Om4IJ4.summary: Lex Fridman interviews chip architect Jim Keller about the future of computing, AI, life and consciousness. Topics include CPU design, branch prediction and why imperfect designs often win.
G4hL5Om4IJ4.why: Recommended as a stellar long-form interview with someone both very smart and wise, mined for CPU design insights.

GC-0tCy4P1U.summary: Casey Muratori responds on-stream to a dismissive Twitter post by demonstrating how slow Visual Studio's startup and debugger watch window are, comparing it to much older software and machines. It is a long rant about software performance and bloat.
GC-0tCy4P1U.why: HN commenters cite it as the canonical concrete demonstration that modern developer tools got slower despite vastly faster hardware.

Gh-Tff7DdzU.summary: Simon Knowles, co-founder and CTO of Graphcore, talks about "intelligence processors", chips designed specifically for machine learning. The talk was given at the RAAIS 2017 summit and covers Graphcore's architecture.
Gh-Tff7DdzU.why: HN points to it as a technical talk from a chip designer on why AI hardware should put memory close to compute and use async data transfers.

Gj8IA6xOpSk.summary: Clifford Stoll's energetic TED talk, a wandering mix of anecdotes, a science experiment and thoughts on curiosity, education and technology. He is the author of The Cuckoo's Egg.
Gj8IA6xOpSk.why: HN commenters recommend it for Stoll's infectious enthusiasm and his case for teaching kids science, and often mention it in threads about him and his Klein bottles.

GjENnyQupow.summary: A 1996 BBC interview in which Noam Chomsky explains his propaganda model of the media to Andrew Marr, including how filters shape what journalists report and the role of self-censorship.
GjENnyQupow.why: Recommended and quoted in threads on media bias, press and power, and self-censorship.

GsyhGHUEt-k.summary: Tom Scott and Matt Gray talk at Electromagnetic Field about making Emojli, an emoji-only messenger that began as a joke, how it was built and why they never want to do it again.
GsyhGHUEt-k.why: Recommended as an entertaining story of a joke side project growing out of hand, brought up in threads on emoji and side projects.

Gxd23UVID7k.summary: The official audio of Leonard Cohen's 'Everybody Knows' from the album I'm Your Man.
Gxd23UVID7k.why: Commenters name it among their favourite Cohen songs, especially in threads after his death.

GZTr1-Gp74U.summary: Roaring Kitty's July 2020 analysis of GameStop, arguing a bullish deep-value case when the stock was about $4 and short interest exceeded 100%. It covers fundamentals, cash balance and technicals.
GZTr1-Gp74U.why: After the 2021 squeeze, HN cites it as the original thesis behind the GME story and praises its quality.

GnO7D5UaDig.summary: Steve Jobs at Apple's 1997 WWDC, shortly after his return, taking developer questions and describing Apple's direction. He discusses the Newton and says to start from the customer experience and work back to technology.
GnO7D5UaDig.why: Held up as a masterclass in handling a crisis and a hostile Q&A, and quoted for starting from customer experience.

G-lN8vWm3m0.summary: A BBC Horizon clip demonstrating the McGurk effect, where the same audio sounds like different syllables depending on the mouth movements you see. It shows that people integrate visual speech information into what they hear.
G-lN8vWm3m0.why: HN uses it as the standard demonstration that the brain reinterprets perception, in threads on speech, AI audio and illusions.

G5B1mIfQuo4.summary: A roughly two and a half hour YMS video on Kimba the White Lion that investigates the claim that Disney's The Lion King copied it.
G5B1mIfQuo4.why: HN recommends it as the thorough investigation of the Kimba and Lion King controversy, and as a quality benchmark for the reviewer.

GCSXNGc7pfs.summary: Dr. John Campbell reviews studies on vitamin D deficiency and immunity, including links to influenza and COVID-19, with Public Health England advice. He walks through the sources he cites.
GCSXNGc7pfs.why: Cited in COVID-era threads as a physician's evidence-based argument that vitamin D is cheap, low-risk and worth considering.

GDzBE6vz5r0.summary: Destin Sandlin tours a progressive metal stamping factory, showing machines that stamp millions of metal parts and the tooling behind them.
GDzBE6vz5r0.why: Recommended for factory-process fans and as part of a series on how US manufacturing is losing tooling capability.

GJVSDjRXVoo.summary: Steve Mould messes with an automated phone bot by telling it to forget its previous prompts and give him a bolognese recipe. It is a short demo of prompt injection against an AI voice agent.
GJVSDjRXVoo.why: Shared as a funny example of jailbreaking AI voice bots, and as the source of the bolognese prompt-injection phrase.

GKYCA3UsmrU.summary: A short clip of Casey Muratori from Handmade Hero explaining why he rejects the object-oriented mindset and how to move away from it. It is part rant, part programming philosophy.
GKYCA3UsmrU.why: HN shares it as a concise critique of OOP from a respected systems programmer.

GLQyj-kBRdo.summary: A dotScale 2014 talk by Robert Kennedy, a former healthcare.gov SRE who later worked at Google, about the engineering effort to rescue the troubled site. It explains the technical and organizational problems behind the failed launch.
GLQyj-kBRdo.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining first-hand engineer account of what went wrong with healthcare.gov and how it was fixed, including that no one owned the whole site.

GZ5XN_mJE8Y.summary: Benn Jordan examines the role of bots and propaganda accounts on X and other social platforms, including the platform's decline and the influence of Russian operations. It covers more than bots, discussing bias and how the platform changed.
GZ5XN_mJE8Y.why: HN commenters cite it in threads about X, Bluesky and online manipulation as evidence that bots and propaganda are real.

GZadCj8O1-0.summary: A five-minute TED talk by Rob Reid, who introduces Copyright Math, applying entertainment-industry piracy loss claims to produce absurd totals such as an $8 billion iPod.
GZadCj8O1-0.why: HN links it in piracy and copyright-lawsuit threads as a funny short demonstration of how inflated industry damage figures are.

GcfLZSL7YGw.summary: PBS Space Time, together with It's Okay to be Smart and PBS Eons, asks how a universe drifting toward disorder produced something as complex as life. It presents the idea that the laws of physics, through thermodynamics, may actually favor the emergence of life.
GcfLZSL7YGw.why: HN commenters point to it as an accessible pop-science introduction to entropy and the physics of life, including Jeremy England's work.

Gksxu-yeWcU.summary: Nerdwriter1 shows how rearranging the scenes of the film Passengers, so the audience shares the female lead's confusion, would change the movie. It draws on discussion of the original script.
Gksxu-yeWcU.why: HN uses it to illustrate how simply reordering scenes can transform a story.

GlXNVnftaNs.summary: Not Just Bikes explains the Dutch concept of autoluw, or nearly car-free, streets and how it is applied across the Netherlands, with examples from Toronto and Copenhagen. It also covers Amsterdam's move toward a nearly car-free city.
GlXNVnftaNs.why: HN commenters share it as a good overview of car-light street design and its effects in discussions of car-centric cities and the 15-minute city.

Gs790JOeN3Y.summary: An update from the Strange Parts YouTuber on his recovery from a brain injury caused by a metal pipe while filming, and his plans for the channel.
Gs790JOeN3Y.why: HN commenters point people dealing with concussions or brain injuries to it as a hopeful first-hand story of recovery.

Gzj723LkRJY.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson builds a blog engine with Ruby on Rails in 15 minutes, the demo that launched Rails' momentum.
Gzj723LkRJY.why: HN treats it as the model for a compelling developer demo and a benchmark for how simple web development once felt.

G77ev9pks4I.summary: Tantacrul analyzes how stock music in reality TV uses blunt, repeated tropes to manipulate viewers, comparing it to nature documentaries. He ties it to ideas of reification and cultural homogenization.
G77ev9pks4I.why: Recommended as a sharp piece of media criticism by a well-liked music YouTuber, and cited for the concept of reification.

G9n8Xp8DWf8.summary: A George Carlin routine on euphemisms and political correctness, tracing how shell shock became PTSD. The uploader adds context about euphemism in political language.
G9n8Xp8DWf8.why: Cited in threads about renaming and sanitized language as a classic comedic statement of the case against euphemism.

GCMXXXmxG-I.summary: Mobileye co-founder and CTO Amnon Shashua explains what goes into sensing for autonomous driving and whether end-to-end deep learning can work for it. He argues for decomposing the problem.
GCMXXXmxG-I.why: Recommended as an accessible technical explanation of Mobileye's approach, and also cited in disputes over Tesla Autopilot.

GL77oOnrPzY.summary: Theoretical physicist Nima Arkani-Hamed gives a public talk on why spacetime may not be fundamental and what might replace it, including newer approaches to scattering amplitudes.
GL77oOnrPzY.why: Praised as a jargon-light talk on advanced physics that HN cites when arguing spacetime is not fundamental.

GaRurhiK-Lk.summary: SalC1 explains how the seed behind the Minecraft title screen panorama was found, using community effort and the Minecraft@Home project. It covers the search through Beta 1.7.3 world seeds.
GaRurhiK-Lk.why: HN points to it as a mind-blowing seed-cracking story related to other Minecraft RNG reversal work.

Gr7T07WfIhM.summary: Adam Curtis's 2016 BBC documentary arguing that politicians, financiers and technologists retreated into a simplified, fake version of the world because reality became too complex. It ranges across Trump, Brexit, Syria, Surkov's Russia and more.
Gr7T07WfIhM.why: HN points to it for its account of propaganda that sows distrust and confusion, and as a starting point for Adam Curtis's work.

G-2dQoeqVVo.summary: Michael Abrash of Valve explains what affordable VR hardware will be capable of within a couple of years, and describes a prototype showing what that level of hardware can do.
G-2dQoeqVVo.why: Cited for his plain-language explanation of how VR convinces the brain and for resolution and pixel-density figures.

G-J86Ka9MkQ.summary: A short unscientific fire test comparing a massive timber house with an ordinary house. It shows the wood chars and burns slowly while still holding together.
G-J86Ka9MkQ.why: Linked in threads on wood buildings as a vivid demonstration that heavy timber resists fire and keeps structural integrity.

G-lGCC4KKok.summary: A PyCon 2012 talk by early YouTube engineer Mike Solomon on how YouTube scaled its architecture, which is mostly Python.
G-lGCC4KKok.why: HN mostly cites it as evidence that YouTube was built on Python and as background on how it scaled.

G32NYQpvy8Q.summary: Big Clive tears down a smart meter with a wireless modem found among fly-tipped materials. He examines its internals and checks conspiracy claims about microphones, cameras and 5G.
G32NYQpvy8Q.why: Pointed to as a clear look at what is inside a smart meter, including anti-tamper switches and the cellular module.

GA8z7f7a2Pk.summary: Amateur footage from the 2009 Sasquatch music festival in which one person starts dancing alone and a crowd gradually joins in, turning it into a dance party.
GA8z7f7a2Pk.why: Used as the classic example of a lone first follower turning one person's action into a movement, in threads about bystanders and group behavior.

GFE4rkSaKOY.summary: A one-minute 2012 Microsoft television commercial for Internet Explorer 9, set to Alex Clare's 'Too Close'. It pitches a 'more beautiful web' with fast one-click access to favorite sites.
GFE4rkSaKOY.why: HN commenters cite it as an example of Microsoft's surprisingly stylish newer ads and as a contrast to the company's messaging elsewhere.

GFMyMxMYDNk.summary: A video essay on how the editors of Star Wars: A New Hope recut and rearranged the footage to rescue the film. It walks through specific changes that improved pacing and drama.
GFMyMxMYDNk.why: Cited as a compact account of how editing shaped the original Star Wars, though one commenter notes a rebuttal video disputes parts of it.

GMvgtPN2IBU.summary: Drive.ai shows its car driving fully autonomously on a rainy night in Mountain View, with heavy downpour, glare, a four-way stop and a broken traffic light.
GMvgtPN2IBU.why: Used in Who's Hiring posts as the company's demo and in self-driving threads as a notable bad-weather example.

GNG6ZzDh9C8.summary: A 12-minute clip from Joe Rogan's podcast in which former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman describes working for Elon Musk at SpaceX. He discusses Musk's engineering breadth, his Mars-focused decision making and the stress of the job.
GNG6ZzDh9C8.why: HN uses it as a firsthand account from an astronaut who worked with Musk, cited in arguments about Musk's engineering ability and SpaceX culture.

GW0rj4sNH2w.summary: Tom Occhino and Jordan Walke present how Facebook builds JavaScript apps, in the talk where React was first publicly announced at JSConf US 2013.
GW0rj4sNH2w.why: Cited as the original React presentation and to credit Jordan Walke as its creator.

GctxvSPIfr8.summary: Jon Gjengset's 2020 PhD dissertation presentation at MIT on partial state in dataflow-based materialized views, the idea behind the Noria database. The Q&A is cut out.
GctxvSPIfr8.why: HN points to it, including Gjengset himself, as a more digestible way into partially-stateful dataflow than the thesis text, mostly in caching and database threads.

Gk-9Fd2mEnI.summary: A 1992 MIT Sloan talk and Q&A by Steve Jobs, then CEO of NeXT, covering NeXT's strategy, co-creating Apple, his ouster, and the value of direct experience. It ranges across technology, business and career advice.
Gk-9Fd2mEnI.why: HN cites it as a primary source for Jobs's own views, pulling timestamps on topics like consultants, objects, NeXT's factory and Apple retail.

GqCwLjhb4YY.summary: Linus Tech Tips covers Intel's CES 2024 demos, focusing on Thunderbolt Share and Wi-Fi 7 improvements.
GqCwLjhb4YY.why: HN links it as one of the few videos showing Thunderbolt Share in action.

GwRRSJ_wtIg.summary: A 39-minute BBC documentary, built from earlier British Transport Films footage, on how the London Underground's Victoria Line was dug in the 1960s.
GwRRSJ_wtIg.why: Mentioned as a fun old documentary and as an example of fast track work and of period BBC presentation.

GwzN5YwMzv0.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains how special relativity leads to the block universe, in which past, present and future all exist equally, and asks what that means for whether the past still exists.
GwzN5YwMzv0.why: HN commenters share it as a clear explanation of the block universe and relativity of simultaneity.

GyFkWb903aU.summary: A Bankless podcast interview with Paul Christiano of the Alignment Research Center on the AI alignment problem and possible solutions. It also covers his views on how an AI takeover might unfold.
GyFkWb903aU.why: HN links it as a balanced, full-length interview with a leading alignment researcher on AI risk.

GyV_UG60dD4.summary: Weird Al's whiteboard-animated music video parodying corporate buzzword culture, from the album Mandatory Fun. The lyrics are packed with business jargon.
GyV_UG60dD4.why: Mostly posted as a joke in threads about corporate-speak, buzzwords and meeting culture.

G2vIdPmsnTI.summary: An OpenZFS office hours session with ZFS co-creator Matt Ahrens answering questions on topics such as hole birth time, send/receive buffers, device removal, block pointer rewrite and performance with many snapshots.
G2vIdPmsnTI.why: Cited as the authoritative explanation of why block pointer rewrite is so hard to implement in ZFS.

G2y8Sx4B2Sk.summary: A brief clip of Inigo Montoya from The Princess Bride saying 'You keep using that word. I do not think it means what you think it means.'
G2y8Sx4B2Sk.why: Used purely as a joke reply when someone misuses a term.

G6D1YI-41ao.summary: The Monty Python sketch in which a man uses a mistranslated Hungarian phrasebook with absurd results, followed by the courtroom scene.
G6D1YI-41ao.why: Used purely as a joke reference to bad translation and phrasebooks.

G9D8dzl4zGk.summary: A short Global News report on the Pentagon confirming a $22 million UFO investigation program and releasing Navy infrared footage from the 2004 Nimitz encounter.
G9D8dzl4zGk.why: HN cites it as the source of the released UFO footage, though commenters often debate whether the video shows anything beyond camera artifacts.

GEZhD3J89ZE.summary: Apple's WWDC 2020 keynote covering iOS, iPadOS, watchOS, privacy, tvOS and macOS, and the announcement of the move of Macs to Apple silicon. It includes demos of Rosetta translation and virtualization on ARM.
GEZhD3J89ZE.why: HN cites it as the primary source for what Apple announced about the Apple silicon transition, Docker and Safari extensions.

GEmuEWjHr5c.summary: Veritasium argues that every new technology, from motion pictures to TV, was predicted to revolutionize education and none did. It asks what actually could, drawing on the host's physics education research.
GEmuEWjHr5c.why: HN cites it in education and AI threads as a history of failed technology-will-transform-teaching predictions.

GGgiGtJk7MA.summary: A five-minute Sky News interview clip from June 2016 in which Michael Gove says Britons have had enough of experts. It was archived for use in a news report.
GGgiGtJk7MA.why: Used to check the quote in context, since the full sentence referred to experts who are consistently wrong, and as a jibe in Brexit threads.

GI5kwSap9Ug.summary: A segment from the animated film The Twelve Tasks of Asterix, in which Asterix must get Permit A 38 from a maze-like building run by unhelpful bureaucrats. He wins by asking for a nonexistent permit.
GI5kwSap9Ug.why: HN commenters reference it as the famous satire of bureaucracy, including as the name for an SSH key management tool.

GTJ3LIA5LmA.summary: A Mr. Show sketch, 'Blow Up the Moon', in which characters cheerfully argue for blowing up the moon.
GTJ3LIA5LmA.why: Used purely as a joke reference in threads about the moon, Project A119 and big dumb ideas.

GYkq9Rgoj8E.summary: Apple's full WWDC 2023 keynote, covering the 15-inch MacBook Air, new Mac hardware, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS and the unveiling of Apple Vision Pro. It runs about two hours.
